description: São Paulo healthtech using AI and data integration to detect billing fraud, waste, and procedure-authorization errors in Brazil's private healthcare claims system. Platform has processed over $25B in claims; revenue and client base grew 4x in the past year.
current_status: Largest Series A in Brazilian healthcare sector history. Deployed across operadoras (health-plan payers) with documented 25% productivity lift in auditing/billing within 6 months of adoption. Deploying capital into AI models for procedure authorization and further integration with operadora IT systems.

founder.name: Rafael Tinoco + Fabrício Valadão
founder.background: Founders came out of Brazilian healthcare claims and payer operations — deep operadora-side knowledge of where billing fraud actually leaks. Built Arvo from inside the domain, not as an outside tech play.
founder.problem_fit: HIGH. The problem (R$40B+ leaked annually to waste and fraud) was learned from inside the payer system. Data moat of $25B processed claims couldn't have been built by an outsider.
founder.execution_evidence: Processed $25B in claims, 4x revenue and client-base growth in 12 months, landed largest Series A in Brazilian healthcare history.
founder.red_flags: Top-10 operadora contracts still pending — sales execution through 18-month procurement cycles is the pending adversity test.

stage_context.vs_base: Arvo's $25B processed-claims data moat and operadora contract model justify strong thriving skew (+18pp) — the single largest positive delta in the portfolio at this stage. Breakout (+8pp) contingent on top-3 operadora wins and regulatory acceptance of AI-based denials.

verdict: Arvo survives IF (a) at least 3 top-10 operadoras sign multi-year contracts by end of 2026 (stickiness is everything in healthcare payer tech), (b) ANS regulatory scrutiny on AI-based claim denials does not force a model audit that slows sales, (c) competing AI tools from US healthcare-claims vendors (Cohere Health, Optum) do not enter Brazil via partnership. Most fragile: (a) — top-10 operadoras move at 18-month procurement cadence and one delayed contract can stall growth.
top_risk: Regulatory risk from ANS: if AI-driven claim denials get flagged, operadoras pause deployments and sales cycle triples overnight
top_opportunity: Brazilian operadoras lose R$40B+ annually to fraud and waste (IESS 2024); Arvo's data moat from $25B processed claims creates genuine defensibility against AI entrants
